newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-VAN GAAL TO QUIT AJAX AND "SPREAD HIS WINGS".
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VAN GAAL TO QUIT AJAX AND "SPREAD HIS WINGS".

text.p: Louis van Gaal, architect of Dutch champion's Ajax Amsterdam's greatest triumphs, announced on Thursday he will leave the club at the end of the season.
Van Gaal, 45, took over as coach from Leo Beenhakker in September 1991. In his first season he led the club to the UEFA Cup.

Since then Ajax have won trophies galore -- three league titles, the European Champions' Cup, Dutch and European Super Cups and the World Club Cup -- and have set new standards for top European soccer.
Last season Ajax just failed to retain their European crown, losing to Juventus on penalties in Rome. In 52 "international" games under Van Gaal, previously assistant coach, Ajax lost only six times.
"I've achieved everything I can with Ajax. I now want to spread my wings," Van Gaal told a news conference at Ajax's towering new Arena stadium -- another legacy to the successes he brought the club.
"My contract expires (at the end of the current season) so I have the chance to make that step."
Van Gaal said he did not have a new club to go to, and Ajax chairman Michael Van Praag said no successor had been lined up.
"I have told Ajax (my decision to leave) early out of respect for the club," Van Gaal said, adding that he was certain to head away from the Netherlands.
"My ambitions lie abroad. I would like to go to a club comparable to Ajax."
Despite Ajax's current position in the Dutch first division -- an unaccustomed sixth -- Van Gaal's availability on the European managerial merry-go-round will interest several top clubs.
Spanish giants Barcelona have been reported as saying they want Van Gaal as coach, with new recruit Bobby Robson moving up to technical director next season.
Amsterdam-born Van Gaal joined Ajax in 1988.

Largely credited with developing and expanding the club's much-vaunted youth policy -- which over the years has spawned Johan Cruyff, Johan Neeskens, Marco van Basten, Frank Rijkaard, Dennis Bergkamp and Patrick Kluivert, to name but a few -- Van Gaal earned a reputation for discipline on and off the field.
He governed the club and its players like the headmaster he initially trained to be.
Tall, uncompromising and a larger-than-life personality, Van Gaal was often scathing of the press, rounding on journalists in public and not suffering fools gladly.
A journeyman footballer, he played for Ajax, primarily in the reserves, FC Antwerp in Belgium, Telstar Beverwijk, Sparta Rotterdam and AZ Alkmaar.
